Sam —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. Quick read-through from product/strategy perspective: we’re sympathetic to ACME’s desire to productize outputs that are solely derived from their inputs, but we can’t accept a blanket assignment of model outputs or a permanent transfer of training rights. High-level options we can offer: 

1) Scoped productization license — a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use, modify, and distribute outputs generated from Customer Content for productization, limited to the customer’s identified product lines and excluding training the underlying Redwood models.

2) Training opt-in — Redwood will not use Customer Content to retrain base models or internal continuous training pipelines unless the customer explicitly opts in via a separate agreement. We can offer a short standardized opt-in addendum for customers who want that.

3) Feedback license — we can accept a limited feedback license that permits improvements derived from bug reports/feedback, but it must be non-exclusive and exclude transfer of any Customer IP. We can propose specific language.

If ACME needs assignment language for certain narrow deliverables (e.g., a bespoke fine-tuned model we build exclusively for them) we can evaluate case-by-case with commercial terms.

Laura — could you prepare suggested redline snippets for the Order Form/MSA matching options above (inline replies preferred). Ben — can you indicate whether we have flexibility on credits/one-off concessions if they insist on stronger rights?

I’ll keep ACME updated but want to align legal + commercial before we send firm countertext.

—Jonas
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Jonas — forwarding inline suggestions. I reviewed ACME’s PDF and drafted three short replacement clauses that map to the options you outlined. Below are the suggested redlines; feel free to paste into the Order Form/Exhibit A as appropriate.

---Quoted message---
On Tue, Aug 17, 2026 at 2:02 PM Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@acme.com> wrote:
> Jonas / Laura —
>

> - Feedback license: They want a permanent, royalty-free license for feedback-derived improvements (narrowly scoped to avoid host-model reveal).

(End quote)

Inline replacements (pick one per category):

1) Output/Productization
Option A (Permissive license — recommended): 
"Customer shall have a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable right to use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative works of Outputs that are solely and directly generated by the Service from Customer Content in connection with Customer’s internal product(s) identified in the Order Form; provided that such Outputs shall not grant Customer any rights to Redwood’s pre-existing or independently developed Models or underlying weights, nor permit Customer to use such Outputs to train third-party or Redwood models."

Risk: preserves Redwood model IP while giving ACME meaningful product rights.

2) Training / Data Use
Proposed Clause: 
"Redwood shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any Redwood models, sub-models, or derivative training datasets without Customer’s prior written consent via a separate addendum. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use de-identified, aggregated telemetry for service reliability and abuse detection, provided such use cannot be reverse-engineered to recreate Customer Content."

3) Feedback License
Narrow License Draft: 
"Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use Feedback (as defined in the Agreement) solely to improve the Service; such license excludes Customer Confidential Information and does not permit Redwood to grant third parties rights under Customer Confidential Information or to claim ownership over Customer Content-derived Outputs."

Commercial/operational asks: 
- If ACME insists on assignment or permanent transfer for Outputs beyond the Option A license above, recommend requiring a commercial premium (term-limited assignment or higher committed spend).
- We should confirm whether procurement needs a legal sign-off matrix for any training opt-in addendum.

I’ve attached an annotated doc with line numbers for their PDF (ACME_MSA_Redlines_annotated.docx). Let me know and I’ll send final language to Sam.

—Laura
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
